# PPI延續債市漲勢，長期資金仍須付出高殖利率

## 通膨舒緩擴及整條殖利率曲線

7月生產者物價低於預期，接續前一天CPI利多，帶動各年期美債上漲。5年期殖利率下跌6個基點至4.32%、降幅最大；2年與10年期各跌5個基點至4.15%及4.63%。$250億30年期標售平穩完成後，30年期殖利率下跌3個基點至5.21%，但得標利率仍為2001年以來最高。

整體PPI月增率持平，年增率由5.5%降至4.7%。能源、食品及運輸成本下滑，顯示部分與伊朗戰爭相關的成本正沿生產鏈消退。數據公布後，花旗、摩根士丹利與Jefferies經濟學家預估7月核心PCE月增0.2%。9月升息機率降至40%以下，但克里夫蘭Fed總裁Hammack仍主張現在就應行動。

10年期殖利率的兩個組成都有貢獻：實質殖利率下跌3個基點至2.39%，損益兩平通膨率下降2個基點至2.24%。股市將消息解讀為Fed更有空間等待，而非衰退警訊。S&P 500上漲0.65%創新高，Nasdaq 100上漲1.15%，信用債基金也走高；油價下跌，進一步支持當日通膨舒緩的定價。

基準殖利率下降之際，融資活動依然密集。AMD完成公司歷來最大筆美元債發行、籌得$47.5億；另一筆$22.5億資料中心債券，則以Jane Street的15年租約支持。據報超大型雲端業者尚未起租的租約已達$1兆，未來現金流承諾遠超出當前發債行事曆。另一端，Telesat新借$1.2億仍難填補舊業務的到期缺口，烏克蘭鐵路調高貨運費率後也尚未脫離違約。債市漲勢降低了折現率，背後的資金需求卻繼續增加。

## PPI降溫，仍未化解Fed內部分歧

PPI年增率下降0.8個百分點，降幅超過預期。能源連續第二個月下跌、跌幅3.1%；食品創年初以來最大降幅，運輸與倉儲成本下跌1.8%，為2023年4月以來最大。核心生產者物價月增0.2%、年增4.2%。週四油價走低，也與數據中運費及投入成本減輕相呼應。

科技產品仍是例外。電子零組件與配件年漲近28%、接近紀錄，電腦及電腦設備價格更創下9.8%的歷史最大漲幅。這與CPI科技類別的表現一致，讓AI投資對物價的影響有了具體數據。投資組合管理費漲幅為一年多來最大，醫院門診費用也明顯上升；醫師服務與住院照護則溫和，機票大跌，貿易服務利潤率在6月上升後回落。

納入PCE計算的項目仍足夠溫和，讓花旗、摩根士丹利與Jefferies預估7月核心月增0.2%。搭配招聘轉弱，這支持央行耐心觀察，但不能據此認定通膨已回到Fed目標。對多數主要貿易夥伴徵收至少10%的進口關稅，加上科技投入成本上升，仍有後續轉嫁空間；就業降溫則讓決策者更有理由先觀察，而非預先承諾政策路徑。

Hammack歡迎近期較低的通膨讀數，卻表示尚無信心物價會持續減速至2%。她週四在俄亥俄州重申，利率不具實質緊縮效果，現在就需要採取行動，延續她在7月反對維持利率、支持升息25個基點的立場。她質疑的是通膨水準與持續性，並不是認為最新數據再度加速。

Barkin則主張，通膨下降支持短期按兵不動，但若物價壓力變得根深蒂固，仍可再緊縮。前達拉斯Fed總裁Kaplan也支持7月暫停，認為9月前應保持開放。他將AI投資、關稅、勞動供給限制與油價列為上行因素，AI應用與中國產能過剩則可能壓低價格。Kaplan目前是高盛副董事長，並非有投票權的決策官員。

殖利率曲線給予政策敏感年期更多舒緩。2年與10年期利差維持48個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大2個基點至106個基點。近一個月2年及5年期殖利率分別下跌11及5個基點，30年期仍上升11個基點。10年期實質殖利率為2.39%、較一個月前高3個基點，30年期實質殖利率為2.97%、高8個基點。下次會議的急迫性降低，並未消除投資人對長期報酬的要求。

其他市場也未同步反應。股市創高，VIX卻小升0.55%至14.63，美元指數僅跌0.09%至99.921。黃金期貨在收盤資料中近乎持平、為$4,415.60，與稍後現貨跌破$4,400屬不同商品及時間點。債市反映的是近期政策壓力減輕，不代表所有市場都由同一因素主導。

## 長債標售順利完成，貨幣市場資金仍充裕

30年期標售得標利率5.216%，較發行前交易利率高不到0.5個基點。投標倍數2.39，接近前六次可比標售平均2.36。長債回吐部分標售前漲幅，收盤殖利率仍約跌3個基點。買家在小幅讓利後消化供給，保留部分PPI帶來的漲勢，政府卻須支付這個年期自2001年以來最高的標售利率。

週三$420億10年期標售得標利率為4.683%，亦創2007年以來最高。兩場標售顯示政府仍可籌到資金，只是條件昂貴，而非債務無人承接。面對持續赤字與通膨不確定性，民間價格敏感型投資人正在吸收更大的債務存量，Fed與外國官方部門提供的結構性需求則較少。

惠譽週四確認美國AA+評等，但警告減稅與關稅退還將使2026年赤字占GDP比重擴大。本財政年度迄今利息支出達$1.17兆，較去年同期增加15%，部分原因正是殖利率上升。30年期房貸利率6.69%、為2025年7月以來最高，也顯示較高利率正在傳入家庭融資。

財政部對未來附息債標售的措辭，由考慮「增加」改為「調整」，讓市場開始期待縮減長債標售；目前並未實際減量。若增加2年至7年期發行，可降低遠端存續期間供給，卻只是重新分配再融資曝險，並不消除借款需求。Kaplan也將長端殖利率視為全球供需的結構性問題，而非單純反映聯邦資金利率。

現券交易活躍。名目附息公債按原始面額計算的成交額增加4.9%至$9,921億；7年至10年期增加25.8%至$2,303億，20年以上增加34.3%至$1,131億。交易商對客戶成交占比分別為46.7%及49.3%。因此標售及收盤漲勢都有相當參與度，但成交總額本身不代表客戶淨買進方向。

貨幣市場未添壓力。Fed在截至9月14日的月度期間不進行準備金管理用途的國庫券購買，仍計畫再投資約$170億。8月12日SOFR為3.62%，低於準備金利率3個基點；8月5日銀行準備金達$3兆，高於年底的$2.85兆。即使國庫券發行增加，現金相對擔保品仍充裕。

準備金管理購買在2025年12月開始時每月約$400億，4月降至$250億、5月降至$100億，目前暫停下一期間購買。這是準備金充足程度的技術判斷，不是重啟量化緊縮，也不是政策利率改變。短期資金寬裕，與標售呈現的長期借款昂貴，可以同時存在。

## AI投資同時增加公司債、專案債務與未來租約

AMD發行$47.5億債券，分成3年至10年的四個年期。最長年期利差由初步討論收窄約25個基點至美債加90個基點。資金可償債或作一般公司用途，包括下月到期的$8.75億債券。截至6月27日，公司債務為$32億，現金與短期投資則達$131億。

AMD已同意對Anthropic投資最高$50億。分析師預估，與Anthropic及微軟的協議擴大需求後，2026年營收可增47%至逾$510億。資產負債表與成長前景有助發行，但這筆規模也代表資料中心、設備、公用事業與政府赤字共同競爭的資金池，又多了一家大型借款人。

Fluidstack與Next Frontier在奧克拉荷馬州合資的Zenith Arc，推出$22.5億5年期優先擔保綠色債券，穆迪評等Ba2。資金支持約149MW運算設施與變電站。Jane Street子公司簽下15年絕對三重淨租約，除基本租金外，承擔營運成本、稅金、水電、保險及電力，並由Jane Street Group提供慣常保證。租約把相當部分營運責任交給租戶，但專案仍屬非投資級。

這筆交易與Jane Street週三自身的$146億擔保發行不同：同一家公司既是企業借款人，也成為另一發行人基礎設施收入的合約來源。Edged Compute今年已發行$13億綠債，TeraWulf為資料中心籌得$32億。這類專案的永續發行額由2024年$76億升至2025年$112億。綠色標籤可能拓展買家，但施工、供電、技術及租戶集中度仍決定信用風險。

未來租約顯示，負擔比眼前的發債行事曆更大。Amanda Lynam領軍的高盛分析團隊估計，超大型雲端業者已認列的租約承諾約$2,000億，另有$1兆尚未起租租約揭露於財報附註，後者在不到一個月內由$7,250億增加。這些租約要等使用與付款開始才認列為租賃負債，卻已代表未來現金流支出，以及在進駐前必須籌措建設融資的設施。

其他高品質發行人也在與這批供給競爭。法國巴黎銀行發現，LVMH、Sanofi及BAE Systems等歐洲企業，即使未直接涉入資料中心，其CDS仍較年底上升逾10%。全球投資級公司債利差約80個基點，僅比今年稍早的金融危機後低點高約6個基點。大型且流動性佳的雲端業者新債，可能吸走其他低利差債券的需求，即使那些公司的營運並未惡化。

週四報酬仍然平穩。LQD上漲0.41%，HYG與JNK分別漲0.23%及0.20%，EMB漲0.44%。長天期公司債指數上漲約0.64%至0.66%，接近長天期美債的0.61%。基準殖利率下降貢獻不少，個別定價則顯示，市場仍提供資金，只是條件各異。

## 新貸款與費率調升，仍未填補重整缺口

Telesat借入$1.2億作一般公司用途，同時其傳統地球同步軌道衛星業務營收下滑25%、營業虧損C$1,270萬。未來14個月四筆到期債務約$21億，包括12月的$13.2億定期貸款與$3.87億擔保債券、明年6月的$2.25億擔保債券，以及2027年10月的$2.13億無擔保債務。公司表示，現金流與現金儲備不足以支應。

去年重組將私人貸款的擔保範圍放在Telesat GEO，而非新的低軌道業務，引發仍在進行的債權人訴訟。管理層預期能處理到期債務、讓GEO持續經營，但申報文件對12月償付能力提出重大疑慮。含選擇權在內、最高C$27億的15年加拿大軍方合約，以及可望取得的$1.89億美國頻譜重分配款項，支持的是整體企業，並不等於已備妥舊業務近期到期款。股價週四下跌13.4%。

烏克蘭鐵路得到的是新的收入措施，而非違約解決方案。8月初貨運費率上調30%，低於申請的45%。這家國營公司4月談判失敗後，正為$11億債券準備另一份提案；1月已停止付息，上月約$7億到期未償，其餘於2028年到期。另提議2027年1月再調高費率15%，尚未獲准。

前次方案包含本金減記20%、依貨運量調整的機制、延長至2033年、分期攤還，以及隨時間提高票息。提高費率改善談判基礎，但戰損、修繕、能源與人事成本、貨運量下降，以及虧損的客運服務仍在拖累。正式談判尚未重啟，債權人目前可評估的是較好的營運條件，不是已議定的重整或恢復付款。

## 日本靠近升息，其他央行各有政策限制

據報日本政府支持日本銀行近期升息，可能在9月或10月；日圓疲弱、干預效果消退，使雙方立場靠近。這與前一天描述的政策拉鋸有所不同。交易員對9月18日升息的定價達74%，10年期日債殖利率小升至2.87%，接近上月的三十年高點。政策利率仍為1%，遠低於Fed的3.5%至3.75%區間。

7月企業物價年增7.2%，僅略低於6月修正後的7.3%；月增0.1%，6月則上修至0.5%。石油、煤、化學品及非鐵金屬帶動年度漲幅。上半年通膨相關企業破產556件，為2018年開始統計以來最多，7月再創單月121件紀錄。弱日圓、能源與AI機械需求，持續推高投入成本。

政府訊號一度推升日圓，匯率卻收在每美元159.50，為7月30日以來最弱，接近過去曾引發干預的160區域。市場目光正從下一次是否升息，轉向後續速度。加快正常化有助匯率與資金留在國內，但6月家庭支出已連續第七個月下降，央行也不能忽略成長。

挪威連續第二次維持存款利率4.25%，符合全部16位受訪分析師預期，未發布新預測。總裁Ida Wolden Bache表示，兩次溫和核心通膨讀數值得多觀察，尚不足以認定前景已實質改變。薪資成長與緊俏勞動市場，使再次升息仍有可能。交換市場對9月及年底前的升息定價分別為12與22個基點，低於前一天的15與27個基點。

土耳其把年底通膨預測由26%上修至28%，更接近市場調查29%。總裁Fatih Karahan承認先前預測部分未能達成。7月通膨降至31.8%，能源不確定性卻使央行持續以40%隔夜利率供應資金，而非已暫停的37%一週附買回利率。2026年正式目標仍為24%，新的2027年預測與目標均為15%。何時恢復附買回融資須視市場情況，因此預測更新尚未帶來較寬鬆的實際操作。

越南受限於銀行資金。央行指出，越南盾貸款超過存款約VND2,000兆、約$768億。政府追求下半年近12%成長，希望降低貸款成本，包括優惠方案至少比銀行同類年期平均利率低1個百分點。越南國家銀行卻警告，流動性、利率、匯率與金融穩定，已讓貨幣支持空間非常有限。

銀行轉向海外找資金，Techcombank推出$10億聯貸。央行今年信用成長目標約15%，7月CPI年增4.45%；若要讓2026年平均通膨接近4.5%，餘下月份平均月增率只能約0.34%。貸款已高於存款，再壓低放款利率，可能只是將壓力轉向資金成本與匯率，而非消除限制。

## 接著看PCE、實際油流與兩個海外決策

8月26日7月核心PCE、其間的就業數據及Kevin Warsh的傑克森洞發言，將檢驗等待的理由。若月增接近經濟學家預估0.2%、招聘持續降溫，且指引支持7月按兵不動，政策敏感年期將較受惠。服務通膨擴散、勞動數據轉強，或更強調央行公信力，則可能使Hammack的主張重新獲得支持。

油價舒緩須落實到運輸。週四WTI下跌2.33%至$81.33，布蘭特下跌2.10%至$87.11。荷莫茲持續通航、運費與保險成本下降，才能讓7月能源與運輸降價更持久；新攻擊、持續關閉或油價再漲，可能帶動2年期殖利率與通膨補償同步上升。單靠談判標題，尚不足以確認任一方向。

印尼8月14日預算演說是眼前的財政考驗。赤字路徑須可信且符合3%法定上限，低於2.5%的目標及較低淨發債量較有利市場。若赤字為2.2%，2027年預估淨發債可降至IDR722兆，即使總發行仍增至IDR1,750兆。這些是附帶條件的推估，不是已宣布的預算結果。

日本9月18日會議則在較遠處。政府支持、7.2%企業物價漲幅及接近160的日圓，都有利升息，但會後路徑指引同樣重要。印尼落實財政約束、日本政策跟進，可支持本地資產並與美元長債競爭；若落空，壓力便可能更多留在匯率與當地長端殖利率。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
# PPI extends the bond rally, while long debt still commands a high yield

## Inflation relief reaches the whole curve

Treasuries rallied across maturities after July producer prices came in softer than expected, adding to the previous day's CPI relief. Five-year yields fell the most, down 6 basis points to 4.32%; two- and ten-year yields dropped 5 to 4.15% and 4.63%. The 30-year declined 3 to 5.21% after a $25 billion auction cleared without major disruption, but at its highest awarded yield since 2001.

Headline PPI was unchanged on the month and slowed to 4.7% annually from 5.5%. Cheaper energy, food and transport suggested that some costs associated with the Iran war were receding through the production chain. Economists at Citigroup, Morgan Stanley and Jefferies put July core PCE at a 0.2% monthly increase after the release. September hike odds fell below 40%, though Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack still argued for action now.

Both components of ten-year yields contributed: real yields fell 3 basis points to 2.39% and breakevens 2 to 2.24%. Stocks treated the news as more room for the Fed to wait rather than a warning of recession. The S&P 500 gained 0.65% to a record, Nasdaq 100 rose 1.15%, and credit funds advanced. Oil also declined, reinforcing the day's inflation relief.

Lower benchmark yields met a busy financing market. AMD raised $4.75 billion, its largest dollar bond sale, and a separate $2.25 billion data-center offering relied on a 15-year Jane Street lease. Hyperscalers' uncommenced leases reportedly reached $1 trillion, adding future cash-flow obligations beyond today's bond calendar. Meanwhile, Telesat's new $120 million loan did little to resolve its legacy maturities, and Ukrainian Railways remained in default despite higher freight tariffs. The rally reduced discount rates; the financing needs behind them continued to grow.

## Softer producer prices do not settle the Fed debate

PPI's 0.8-percentage-point annual slowdown was larger than expected. Energy fell 3.1%, its second monthly decline, food recorded its biggest drop since the start of the year, and transportation and warehousing costs fell 1.8%, the most since April 2023. Core producer prices increased 0.2% monthly and 4.2% annually. Thursday's cheaper crude added a market signal to the reported easing in freight and input costs.

Technology remained an exception. Electronic components and accessories were almost 28% more expensive than a year earlier, close to a record pace, while computer and computer-equipment prices rose a record 9.8%. Those increases echoed CPI's technology categories and connected AI investment to a visible inflation channel. Portfolio-management fees had their largest increase in more than a year, and hospital outpatient care rose sharply. Physician services and inpatient care were tame, airfares fell heavily and trade-service margins retreated after June's increase.

The components feeding PCE were soft enough for Citigroup, Morgan Stanley and Jefferies to project a 0.2% July core increase. That would support patience alongside weaker hiring, not establish a return to the Fed's inflation objective. Tariffs of at least 10% on imports from most major trading partners and higher technology-input costs still leave room for pass-through. The employment slowdown argues for observing that process rather than committing in advance.

Hammack welcomed the recent lower readings but said they did not give her confidence inflation would slow sufficiently to reach 2%. Speaking in Ohio on Thursday, she maintained that rates were not meaningfully restrictive and that action was needed now, repeating her preference for the quarter-point increase she supported in dissenting against July's hold. Her objection concerns the level and persistence of inflation, not a claim that the latest report accelerated.

Barkin has made the near-term case for holding steady as inflation declines, while retaining the option to tighten if price pressure becomes embedded. Former Dallas Fed President Robert Kaplan also endorsed July's hold and urged an open mind through September. He pointed to AI investment, tariffs, labor constraints and oil as upward influences, against AI adoption and Chinese overcapacity pulling the other way. Kaplan now speaks as a Goldman Sachs vice chairman, not a voting policymaker.

The curve gave policy-sensitive maturities more relief than the long bond. The 2s10s slope stayed at 48 basis points; 2s30s widened 2 to 106. Over a month, two- and five-year yields are down 11 and 5 basis points, while the 30-year is still up 11. Ten-year real yields remain 3 basis points higher at 2.39%, and 30-year real yields 8 higher at 2.97%. A less urgent next meeting has not removed the longer-term return investors require.

Other markets did not respond uniformly. VIX edged up 0.55% to 14.63 despite record equities, and the Dollar Index fell only 0.09% to 99.921. Gold futures were nearly unchanged at $4,415.60 in the closing snapshot, distinct from later spot trading below $4,400. The bond rally reflected less immediate policy pressure without eliminating differences across instruments and trading windows.

## The long auction clears; funding markets remain comfortable

The 30-year sale stopped at 5.216%, less than half a basis point above its when-issued yield. Bid-to-cover was 2.39, close to the 2.36 average of the preceding six comparable auctions. The long bond gave back some pre-sale gains but finished about 3 basis points lower in yield. Buyers took the supply at a small concession and retained part of the PPI rally, with the government paying its highest auction rate on this maturity since 2001.

Wednesday's $42 billion ten-year sale had cleared at 4.683%, its highest since 2007. Together, the auctions show market access at expensive terms rather than a failure to place debt. Private, price-sensitive investors are absorbing a larger stock amid deficits and uncertainty about inflation, with less structural support from the Fed and foreign official holders.

Fitch affirmed the US at AA+ on Thursday but warned that tax cuts and tariff rebates would widen the deficit relative to GDP in 2026. Fiscal-year-to-date interest expense reached $1.17 trillion, up 15% from a year earlier, partly because yields themselves have risen. A 30-year mortgage rate of 6.69%, the highest since July 2025, shows how those rates also reach household financing.

Treasury's shift from discussing future coupon-sale “increases” to “changes” has raised the possibility of smaller long-bond auctions. No reduction has occurred. Moving more issuance into two- to seven-year notes could reduce far-end duration supply but would redistribute refinancing exposure, not eliminate borrowing. Kaplan described long yields as a structural global supply-demand issue rather than simply a reflection of fed funds.

Trading was active. Nominal-coupon volume rose 4.9% to $992.1 billion in original-face value. Seven- to ten-year activity increased 25.8% to $230.3 billion and turnover beyond 20 years rose 34.3% to $113.1 billion. Dealer-to-customer shares were 46.7% and 49.3%, respectively. The auction and closing rally therefore occurred with substantial participation, although turnover does not identify net customer demand.

Money markets supplied no additional stress. The Fed will make no reserve-management bill purchases in the monthly period ending September 14, while still planning roughly $17 billion of reinvestment purchases. SOFR fixed at 3.62% on August 12, 3 basis points below interest on reserve balances. Reserves stood at $3 trillion on August 5, up from $2.85 trillion at year-end, and cash remained abundant relative to collateral despite more bill issuance.

Reserve-management purchases began near $40 billion a month in December 2025, fell to $25 billion in April and $10 billion in May, and are now paused for the coming period. This is a judgment about ample reserves, not a return to quantitative tightening or a change in the policy rate. It separates comfortable near-term funding from the expensive long-duration borrowing exposed by the auctions.

## AI investment adds bonds, project debt and future leases

AMD issued $4.75 billion across four tranches from three to ten years. Its longest spread tightened about 25 basis points from initial discussion to 90 over Treasuries. Proceeds may repay debt or fund general corporate uses, including an $875 million maturity next month. As of June 27, the company had $3.2 billion of debt against $13.1 billion of cash and short-term investments.

The chipmaker has agreed to invest up to $5 billion in Anthropic. Analysts estimate 47% revenue growth in 2026 to more than $51 billion as Anthropic and Microsoft agreements broaden demand. Its balance sheet and growth outlook helped the four-tranche sale, while the size adds another borrower to the capital pool financing data centers, equipment, utilities and government deficits.

Zenith Arc, an Oklahoma venture between Fluidstack and Next Frontier, offered $2.25 billion of five-year senior-secured green bonds rated Ba2 by Moody's. The financing supports a compute facility and substation totaling about 149 megawatts. A Jane Street subsidiary signed a 15-year absolute triple-net lease covering base rent, operating costs, taxes, utilities, insurance and power, with a customary Jane Street Group guaranty. The lease assigns substantial operating obligations to the tenant, but the project remains below investment grade.

This is separate from Jane Street's own $14.6 billion secured issue on Wednesday. The firm is both a corporate borrower and the contractual revenue anchor for another issuer's infrastructure. Edged Compute has sold $1.3 billion of green debt this year and TeraWulf secured $3.2 billion for data centers. Sustainable issuance for such projects reached $11.2 billion in 2025, versus $7.6 billion in 2024. The green label may broaden buyers; construction, power, technology and tenant concentration still determine the credit.

Future leases make the obligations larger than the current bond calendar alone suggests. Goldman Sachs analysts led by Amanda Lynam estimated about $200 billion of recognized hyperscaler lease commitments and another $1 trillion of uncommenced leases disclosed in footnotes. The latter rose from $725 billion in less than a month. They become recognized lease liabilities when use and payments begin, but already represent prospective claims on cash flow and facilities requiring construction finance before occupancy.

Other high-quality issuers are competing with that supply. BNP Paribas found that CDS on European companies including LVMH, Sanofi and BAE Systems had risen more than 10% since year-end despite no direct data-center role. Global investment-grade bond spreads were near 80 basis points, only about 6 above their post-financial-crisis low earlier this year. Large, liquid hyperscaler issues can draw demand away from other tight-spread credits without any deterioration in those companies' operations.

Thursday's returns nevertheless remained orderly. LQD gained 0.41%, HYG 0.23% and JNK 0.20%; EMB rose 0.44%. Long corporate indexes gained about 0.64%–0.66%, close to long Treasuries' 0.61%. Benchmark relief did much of the work, while individual pricing showed that borrowers could still obtain capital on differentiated terms.

## New money and higher tariffs leave restructuring gaps

Telesat borrowed $120 million for general corporate purposes as its legacy geostationary-satellite business reported a 25% revenue decline and C$12.7 million operating loss. About $2.1 billion falls due across four tranches over the next 14 months: a $1.32 billion term loan and $387 million secured note in December, a $225 million secured note next June and $213 million unsecured debt in October 2027. The company said cash flow and reserves do not cover those obligations.

Last year's reorganization placed private loans against Telesat GEO rather than the new low-Earth-orbit business, prompting an ongoing creditor lawsuit. Management expects to address maturities and preserve GEO as a going concern, but the filing identified substantial doubt over December payments. A 15-year Canadian military contract worth up to C$2.7 billion including options, and eligibility for $189 million from US spectrum repurposing, support the wider enterprise without themselves funding the imminent legacy maturities. Shares fell 13.4% Thursday.

Ukrainian Railways gained a new revenue measure, not a resolution of its default. A 30% freight-tariff increase took effect at the start of August, short of the 45% requested. The state company is preparing another proposal for $1.1 billion of bonds after April talks failed. It stopped paying interest in January and did not repay about $700 million due last month; the balance matures in 2028. Another proposed 15% tariff increase for January 2027 is unapproved.

The previous proposal included a 20% principal reduction, freight-volume adjustment mechanism, extension to 2033, amortization and coupons rising over time. Higher tariffs improve the basis for discussions, but war damage, repair bills, energy and labor costs, lower freight volume and a loss-making passenger service continue to weigh. Formal talks have not restarted. Creditors have a better operating input to consider, not an agreed restructuring or restored payments.

## Japan moves toward a hike as other central banks face different limits

Japan's government was reported to support a near-term BOJ increase, likely in September or October, as yen weakness and fading intervention effects brought the authorities closer together. That is a change from the policy tension described a day earlier. Traders assigned a 74% probability to a September 18 increase; the ten-year yield edged up to 2.87%, near last month's three-decade high. The policy rate remains 1%, well below the Fed's 3.5%–3.75% range.

July corporate-goods prices rose 7.2% annually, only slightly below June's revised 7.3%, and 0.1% monthly after June was revised to 0.5%. Oil, coal, chemicals and nonferrous metals led annual pressure. Inflation-related bankruptcies reached 556 in the first half, the most since records began in 2018, followed by a monthly record of 121 in July. A weak yen, energy and AI machinery demand continue to raise input costs.

The yen briefly strengthened on the government signal but closed at 159.50 per dollar, its weakest since July 30 and near the 160 area associated with past intervention. Attention is moving beyond the next hike to the subsequent pace. Faster normalization could support the currency and retain capital, but household spending fell for a seventh consecutive month in June, limiting the room to disregard growth.

Norway held its deposit rate at 4.25% for a second meeting, as all 16 surveyed analysts expected, without new forecasts. Governor Ida Wolden Bache said two benign core-inflation readings warranted more time, not a conclusion that the outlook had materially changed. Wage growth and a tight labor market leave another increase possible. Swaps priced 12 basis points by September and 22 by year-end, down from 15 and 27 a day earlier.

Turkey raised its year-end inflation forecast from 26% to 28%, closer to a 29% market survey. Governor Fatih Karahan acknowledged a partial failure of earlier projections. July inflation slowed to 31.8%, but energy uncertainty kept funding at the 40% overnight rate rather than the suspended 37% one-week repo rate. The formal 2026 target remains 24%; the new 2027 forecast and target are 15%. Returning to repo funding depends on market conditions, so forecast revisions have not yet brought an easier operating stance.

Vietnam's constraint is bank funding. Dong loans exceed deposits by about VND2 quadrillion, or $76.8 billion, according to the central bank. The government seeks almost 12% growth in the second half and wants cheaper loans, including preferential programs at least 1 percentage point below banks' average comparable rates. The State Bank of Vietnam warned that liquidity, interest rates, the exchange rate and financial stability leave very little scope to help.

Techcombank launched a $1 billion syndicated loan as banks sought offshore funding. The central bank targets about 15% credit growth this year, while July CPI was 4.45% annually. Keeping average 2026 inflation near 4.5% would allow only about 0.34% average monthly increases through year-end. With loans already exceeding deposits, pushing lending rates down could move the strain into funding costs and the currency rather than remove it.

## PCE, physical oil flows and two overseas decisions come next

July core PCE on August 26, intervening employment reports and Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks will test the case for waiting. An increase near the economists' 0.2% projections, continued hiring moderation and guidance supporting July's hold would favor the policy-sensitive sector. Broader service inflation, stronger labor data or greater emphasis on credibility would give Hammack's argument renewed force.

Oil relief needs to become physical. WTI fell 2.33% to $81.33 and Brent 2.10% to $87.11 on Thursday. Sustained Hormuz passage and lower freight and insurance costs would make July's energy and transport declines more durable. New attacks, continued closure or renewed oil gains could instead bring two-year yields and breakevens higher together. Negotiating headlines alone do not establish either outcome.

Indonesia's August 14 budget speech is the immediate fiscal test. A credible path within the legal 3% deficit ceiling is needed; a target below 2.5% and lower net issuance would be supportive. A 2.2% deficit could reduce projected 2027 net issuance to IDR722 trillion even as gross sales rise to IDR1.75 quadrillion. These are conditional projections, not announced budget results.

Japan's September 18 meeting has a longer horizon. Government support, 7.2% producer inflation and a yen near 160 now favor an increase, but guidance beyond that meeting will matter as well. Credible fiscal restraint in Indonesia and policy follow-through in Japan could strengthen local assets and compete with dollar duration; disappointment would leave more pressure on their currencies and long yields.
